name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 partisan lean makes this one of the safest Democratic House seats
Ford's fundraising edge: about $816K raised versus Koppie's $58K and just $42 on hand
Open seat after Danny Davis's retirement removes the incumbent's personal vote

model.rationale: The district's D+34 lean and La Shawn Ford's overwhelming financial advantage over an underfunded Republican outweigh the loss of incumbency, keeping the seat firmly in Democratic column despite the open-seat dynamics.
model.watch: With no polling available, a late surge in Republican visibility or spending, or an unexpectedly strong third-party vote, would be the main ways the margin could narrow.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District, anchored in Chicago, is among the most Democratic House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+34. Danny Davis's retirement creates an open seat, but Democratic nominee La Shawn Ford enters with a large financial edge, having raised more than $800,000, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised about $58,000 and reports just $42 on hand. Outside groups have also spent roughly $2.5 million in the contest.

No public general-election polling is available, and national raters have not flagged the race, so expectations rest on district fundamentals. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent. The open seat costs the party an incumbent's personal vote, but the underlying margin is wide enough that the Democratic nominee remains a heavy favorite to hold the seat in November.
